prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1061; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle that entered on a red signal. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck strain and stiffness, no loss of consciousness. Claimant is not represented by counsel. Explained the claims process and the right to seek legal advice if desired.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant describes neck pain beginning the next morning, rated moderate, with headaches on and off. Claimant has not yet seen a physician and plans to attend an urgent care visit. Advised claimant to keep all medical receipts and records. Photos of vehicle damage received and added to file.

Entry 3: Reviewed the responding officer's report. Officer notes both drivers gave consistent accounts of the signal phase and assigned primary fault to the third-party driver. Third-party carrier contacted to confirm liability position and coverage limits. Carrier acknowledged the claim and assigned its own file number.

Entry 4: Claimant returned call to ask about rental vehicle coverage and whether the injury would be handled under the at-fault party's policy. Explained bodily injury claims are presented to the at-fault carrier and that the claimant may submit medical bills and wage documentation directly. Claimant indicated comfort proceeding without counsel for now and asked for a written summary, which was sent.

Entry 5: Medical documentation received from urgent care showing a diagnosis of cervical strain with a recommended course of physical therapy and anti-inflammatory medication. Records added to file. Claimant reports improvement in range of motion. Recommended follow-up with the claimant in two weeks to review progress and outstanding bills before any settlement discussion.
